age.evidence: adolescent rats were given either 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle on postnatal day (P) 35 and 45... on approximately P125 and P132... A total of 13 adult (>P100) female Long Evans rats

sex.evidence: A total of 65 (33 female, 32 male) Long Evans rats... A total of 13 adult (>P100) female Long Evans rats

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/ml) or distilled water vehicle was administered by gavage of 1 ml/kg... adolescent rats were given either 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle on postnatal day (P) 35 and 45... on approximately P125 and P132, these animals were again administered 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle

group_housing.evidence: Animals received identifying foot tattoos and were pairhoused on P30... All animals were pairhoused

day_night_flipped.evidence: They were kept on a 12 h light/dark cycle (on at 0700 h) with all experiments occurring during the light cycle (between 0900 and 1400 h)

assays.assay_description: Immediately after intragastric gavage of 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle, rats were placed in a recording enclosure (adolescents: ~33×20×15 cm cage; adults: ~56 cm diameter × 30 cm polycarbonate tube) and video recorded for 30 min. HTRs scored by two blinded observers. Performed at P35, P45, adulthood (P125/132) and in adult females across diestrus/proestrus.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/ml) or distilled water vehicle was administered by gavage of 1 ml/kg.

setup_habituation.evidence: Immediately after gavage, adolescents were placed into a ~33 cm × 20 cm x 15 cm cage with a transparent lid and video recorded for 30-min

setup_restrain.evidence: placed into a ~33 cm × 20 cm x 15 cm cage with a transparent lid and video recorded

food_restriction.evidence: no food in HTR recording cage/tube

water_restriction.evidence: no water in HTR recording cage/tube

time_to_assay.evidence: Immediately after gavage... video recorded for 30-min

sample_size.evidence: early adolescence (P35, n = 10-11/treatment/sex), late adolescence (P45, n = 10-11/treatment/sex), and adulthood (>P125, n = 7-10/treatment/sex)

outcomes.summary: 1 mg/kg psilocybin failed to induce head twitches in adolescents (P35, P45) but robustly increased HTRs in adults; adult females showed more HTRs than adult males, and females in diestrus showed more HTRs than females in proestrus. Adolescent pre-exposure did not alter adult HTR responses to psilocybin.
outcomes.statistics: Three-way ANOVA: age×sex×treatment F(2,106)=7.30, p=0.001; age×treatment F(2,106)=30.26, p<0.0001; sex×treatment F(1,106)=6.62, p=0.012; main effect treatment F(1,106)=66.25, p<0.0001; age F(2,106)=61.37, p<0.0001. Estrous: treatment F(1,45)=32.83, p<0.0001; stage F(1,45)=8.396, p=0.0058; diestrus vs proestrus p=0.035.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin treatment increased head twitch responses in adult females (p<0.0001) and adult males (p=0.0024), but did not increase head twitches in either P35 or P45 animals... the number of psilocybin-induced head twitch responses is significantly greater in diestrus compared to proestrus (p=0.035)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: A time course of head twitch responses in adult subjects showed an onset of behavioral effects of psilocybin within 5 min, and that reliable differences between psilocybin and vehicle response can be seen across the 30-min recording period (Supplemental Fig. S2)

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours per rubric

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Each video recording was coded by two observers, blind to treatment

E1_environment_type.evidence: placed into a ~33 cm × 20 cm x 15 cm cage... or a large polycarbonate tube ~56 cm diameter x 30 cm height

E6_spatial.evidence: single cage or single tube without compartments

E7_social_context.evidence: animals placed individually for video recording

D1_continuity.evidence: HTR recorded on P35, P45, P125 and P132 in adolescent study; 4 tests across estrous phases in estrous study

D3_recording_days.evidence: P35, P45, P125, P132 (adolescent cohort) or 4 tests separated by ≥1 week (estrous cohort)

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline HTR recording reported

D5_followup.evidence: on approximately P125 and P132, these animals were again administered 1 mg/kg psilocybin or vehicle... to determine if adolescent treatment with psilocybin affected adult head twitch responses

assays.assay_description: Circular elevated maze (40 inch diameter) with two open and two closed (12-inch walls) arms. Rats placed in center of a closed arm and recorded for 10 min. Time in open arms and entries into open arms scored by Any-Maze.

application_type.evidence: Animals treated with psilocybin or vehicle on P35 and P45 (gavage)

setup_habituation.evidence: Subjects were kept in their home cages for 15 min prior to the test to allow for habituation to the testing room

setup_restrain.evidence: subjects were placed in the center of one of the closed arms and were recorded for 10 min

time_to_assay.evidence: On approximately P90, these animals underwent elevated zero maze testing... adolescent treatment on P35 and P45

outcomes.summary: A single adolescent dose of 1 mg/kg psilocybin (P35 or P45) had no long-term effect on adult anxiety-associated behavior in the elevated zero maze; no significant effects of sex or treatment on time in open arms or number of entries.
outcomes.statistics: Two-way ANOVA: no significant effects of sex, treatment, or interaction on % time in open arms or open-arm entries
outcomes.evidence: Two-way ANOVA of the percentage of time spent in the open areas of the maze (Fig. 3A) found no significant effects of sex or treatment, nor their interaction. In addition, no significant effects of sex or treatment were found on the number of entries into the open areas

B1_num_measures.evidence: Any-Maze video analysis software (v4.99) was used to calculate total time spent in the open arms as well as total entries into the open arms

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Any-Maze video analysis software (v4.99) — position tracking only

E1_environment_type.evidence: circular testing apparatus (diameter = 40 inches) with two open stretches of maze and two closed arms

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM/EZM closed arms not scored as shelter per rubric

E3_bedding.evidence: apparatus cleaned with 1.5% quatricide solution between subjects; no bedding

E6_spatial.evidence: EZM treated like EPM per rubric — open-ended arms, not distinct enclosed compartments

D3_recording_days.evidence: completed elevated zero maze testing on P90/91

D5_followup.evidence: treated with psilocybin or vehicle on P35 and P45... completed elevated zero maze testing on P90/91 (~45-55 days post-treatment)

assays.assay_description: Food-restricted rats trained in standard Med Associates operant chambers with two levers; daily 1-h sessions. After shaping and acquisition (one lever rewarded 80%, other 20%) to criterion (24/30 correct on 2 consecutive days), contingencies were reversed and animals tested up to 21 days. Outcomes: days to acquisition criterion and days to reversal criterion.

application_type.evidence: Animals treated with psilocybin or vehicle on P35 and P45 by gavage

setup_habituation.evidence: Subjects started with a shaping phase where they established that pressing the levers resulted in a sugar pellet reward

setup_restrain.evidence: standard operant chambers; animals freely lever-press

food_restriction.evidence: all food was removed from each cage. After this point, subjects were fed once per day with 3.5% of their free-feeding body weight

time_to_assay.evidence: Beginning on P93, these animals then underwent training and testing for probabilistic spatial reversal learning... adolescent treatment on P35 and P45

outcomes.summary: Adolescent psilocybin exposure did not affect adult behavioral flexibility: no significant differences in rates of initial acquisition or of reversal learning by sex, treatment, or interaction.
outcomes.statistics: Cox Proportional Hazard Model: no significant effects of sex, treatment, or interaction on acquisition or reversal
outcomes.evidence: Cox Proportional Hazard Model... found no significant differences due to subject sex, treatment, nor their interaction... Survival analysis of the rate of reversal learning... again found no effect of sex, treatment, or their interaction

B1_num_measures.evidence: days to acquisition criterion and days to reversal criterion (lever presses on correct vs incorrect lever)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: across-day learning curves, not within-session temporal dynamics

B6_cognitive.evidence: subjects learned that one side resulted in a sugar pellet reward 80% of the time... reversal learning

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med Associates operant chambers — lever-press recording

E1_environment_type.evidence: standard operant chambers (Med Associates, St Albans, VT)

E6_spatial.evidence: single operant chamber compartment with two levers

E8_food_water.evidence: pressing the levers resulted in a sugar pellet reward

D1_continuity.evidence: Each training session lasted 1 h... Trials were stopped at 21 days after reversal

D3_recording_days.evidence: shaping, acquisition to criterion, plus up to 21 days of reversal testing

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline PRL session reported

D5_followup.evidence: Beginning on P93... adolescent treatment on P35 and P45 (~48+ days post-treatment)

judge_notes: Three assays identified: HTR (across age cohorts and estrous study merged into one assay per rubric), Elevated Zero Maze, Probabilistic Reversal Learning.
B2 temporal dynamics for HTR scored Yes based on Supplemental Fig. S2 time course across the 30-min recording.
D3 for HTR: distinct recording days across the adolescent cohort (P35, P45, P125, P132) and estrous cohort (4 separate test days) — falls in 2-7 range.
E6 for EZM: scored 0 (single open space) per rubric note that EPM-like open-ended arms do not count as distinct compartments; overrode qwen's score of 1.

Schedule for psilocybin set to 'repeated' since the same animals received multiple gavage doses across the protocol (adolescent + adult, or 4 estrous tests), though individual within-day administration is acute.
